about: Census for run 2026-11-11-fathers-shelf, step measure: the archive.org scans of the 1841-45 printing of the Catena Aurea in English, the transcriptions, the structure of the printing and of CCEL's transcription, and the share of excerpts the catena build can expect to serve. Measured 2026-11-11 from public downloads; nothing here is served.

measurement_method.layout: ABBYY FineReader XML (_abbyy.gz) parsed streaming (iterparse, peak about 1 MB per file); per page: the running head is the top line; the body column is the commonest line start to the commonest justified right edge; words outside it are margin; small-type lines below the last body-size line are footnotes; lines more than 1.05 times the page's commonest type size are Gospel text.
measurement_method.heads: a run of words flagged smallcaps ending in ";" or "." (or followed by ";")
measurement_method.expected_share: heads of the two copies aligned by (name, printed page); an excerpt counts when the next head also aligns and its words are equal after folding quotes, dropping superscripts, deciding line-end hyphens by the volume vocabulary and removing spaces before punctuation
measurement_method.old_forms: whole-word, case-insensitive counts over each source's text (markup stripped)

findings: The 1841-45 printing is on archive.org in five scan sets (Toronto: Robarts/Trinity AIM-9181, Trinity "43", Kelly AJH-5369, Kelly scribe-2005 items; Saint Mary's College of California; Princeton Theological Seminary). Every volume part has at least two scans of different physical copies of the 1841-45 printing with an ABBYY layout file, so no chapter is left out.

Princeton's Vol. I Part III and Vol. III Part II are the Second Edition of 1865 (title pages read from its OCR), so they are not used; Luke XI-XXIV and Matthew XXII-XXVIII are paired from two Toronto copies.

Heads: the printing sets each head in small capitals, but ends abbreviated heads with a full stop (AUG., CHRYS., GLOSS., THEOPHYL., ID.) and full names with a semicolon (JEROME;, AMBROSE;, BEDE;). In copy A, ";" ends 492 of 1942 heads in Matthew Part I and 100 of 1524 in John Part I. A head rule that needs a semicolon misses most heads; the rule must take the small-capitals name followed by ";" or ".".

Small-capitals runs that are not heads: chapter headings (CHAP. XVI.), signatures (VOL. I.), and margin words (Trinity's John Part I reads the margin "s. 60." as a small-capitals "GO."). Copy A misses heads by not flagging them (golden cases head_missed_by_ocr_copy_a).

Gospel text: the Gospel runs are set in a larger type, but on some pages only slightly larger (OCR sizes 11 against 10.5 in John Part I), so a size ratio of 1.05 misses them; a run crossing a page break changes size and is split. The verse of an excerpt read from the OCR was wrong for many golden entries; the golden verse is read from the page image (and for Matthew and Mark checked against CCEL's verse marks).

Footnotes: most are in a smaller type below the text, in two columns that the OCR can read across each other (John 12:44-50 note e); some are in the body's type size (John 7:14-18 note c). Footnote reference marks are superscripts; the OCR also flags real words as superscript, in both copies at once (John 1:3 "that").

Agreement is not proof: among 154 golden excerpts whose span is the OCR’s, copies A and B gave equal words in 30, and 5 of those differ from the page image: Mark 5:1-20, "&c." read "fyc." by both; Mark 8:22-26, a margin word fused to the text by both; Matthew 26:20-25, a line-end hyphen lost by both (wicked ness); Matthew 25:1-13, a line-end hyphen lost by both (dis course); Matthew 22:15-22, a line-end hyphen lost by both and the ligature æ read as ae by both. The Matthew Part III pair (two Toronto copies, one OCR engine) shares its errors, which also raises its expected share.
Italic capital I is read as "/", "1" or dropped; "&c." as "fyc.", "Sfc.", "8$c." or "$c."; the ligature "æ" as "a", "ae", "g" or "ce". Margin words fuse with the first or last word of a line.

Line-end hyphens: the stated rule (keep where only the hyphenated form occurs in the volume, join where only the joined form occurs, else hold) holds several golden excerpts: money-changer (Luke 1:1-4), seventy-seventh (Luke 3:23-38), never-ending (Matthew 13:24-30), threefold (Matthew 1:1), to-come (John 7:14-18).

The expected served share (excerpts whose head pairs and whose words are equal in both copies, census normalization) is 0.07 to 0.48 of copy A's heads per part (see parts); most excerpts will be held.

Continuation paragraphs: CCEL splits many excerpts into paragraphs that open with no head (1,274 in Matthew); in the printing those run on inside one paragraph (for example the Gloss on Matthew 1:1 and its sentence beginning Generation, he says); the golden keeps such excerpts whole.
Old forms: CCEL's Matthew and Mark keep the printing's forms (shews 250 and 79 against 250 and 80 in the scans); isidore.co's Luke and John are modernized (shews 0).
The edition holds its own list of writers: the Table of Fathers, Doctors, and Commentators printed in Vol. IV (read into authors.json).
